title: Remote HowlPlane Factory observability for persistent Grok roles
problem: Persistent Grok Bots (EM and peers) run in a cloud environment without the live HowlPlane Factory supervisor. Factory campaigns are host-local (XDG state + one supervisor lock; workspace paths on the Owner host under /run/media/system/tallgeese/dev/). howlplane is not on the Grok PATH. HowlBoard can project a ledger slice offline but does not live-observe or dispatch. Installing a second HowlPlane/Factory in the Grok cloud would compete with the active host campaign and is rejected. Without a durable remote coordination surface, EM cannot safely discover active campaigns, see blockers, submit bounded delegated work, or avoid duplicating Factory work.
desired_outcome: EM can (1) discover the active Factory campaign and its status/blockers from authoritative durable state reachable without sharing the Factory host shell, (2) submit bounded implementation work into that Factory without starting a second campaign, (3) receive execution evidence/results into HowlBoard and/or Git, and (4) follow a documented interim protocol until the bridge exists. No second Factory. No raw-provider bypass of HowlFrame.
architecture: Factory remains single-supervisor on the Owner host. Grok roles observe and enqueue via Git- and/or HowlBoard-backed artifacts. HowlPlane may publish a redacted status snapshot and accept owner_direction / queue / backlog admissions that Factory already understands. HowlBoard remains work-state; Plane remains execution-state; Git remains desired org state.
scope: Document interim EM observe/dispatch protocol (HFW runbook)
Smallest durable remote status snapshot from Factory (HowlPlane) OR HowlBoard ingest of published status/ledger slices on a schedule
Document how Grok submits work (Git work item / Pending backlog / factory queue file / owner_direction) that the existing Factory will admit without a second campaign
Wire HFW routing/recovery docs to the remote path (no second runner)
non_goals: Install HowlPlane or start Factory inside the Grok Bot cloud
Share Factory host shell/session with Grok as the steady-state design
Replace HowlBoard or invent a second orchestration runner
Expand authority, weaken approvals/Assurance, or bypass HowlFrame
Compete with open howlplane PR #122 (ecosystem Factory execution) or the 2026-09-27 continuous-improvement campaign
Broad HowlBoard live streaming or multi-tenant Plane SaaS
acceptance_criteria: Runbook names where the active Factory runs (host/workspace evidence) and forbids starting a second Factory from Grok
EM can obtain campaign identity + status/blockers from a durable remote artifact (Git and/or HowlBoard) without SSH into the Factory host
Documented submit path uses an existing Factory admission surface (owner_direction, backlog Pending, factory queue, or equivalent) — verified against howlplane docs/code
Documented evidence return path uses Git PRs/commits and/or HowlBoard LEDGER projection
End-to-end verification: read remote status artifact once published; confirm no second campaign started
orgctl validate still passes; standing budgets unchanged
Implementation of HowlPlane changes is routed through the existing Factory host (--target self/ecosystem) or a still-working governed Plane entrypoint — not a Grok-local Plane install
risk: R2 coordination/observability. No authority, credential, or production-control change. Mis-publishing secrets in status snapshots is a security risk — snapshots must be redacted.
rollback: Revert HFW docs/WI; stop publishing status snapshots; Factory host operation unchanged.

classification.notes: Capability gap is remote observability/submit for non-colocated persistent roles. Not an executor failure. Not fixed by installing Plane on Grok.
